soundness_flags.label: def:one-fixing-certificate and lem:one-fixing-realizability
soundness_flags.one_line: Membership in \(\mathcal K_D(q^\star)\) depends on undefined notions—“one proposed fixing step”, coefficient maps “assembled” from spans, and “retained overlap contractions”—so the lemma's universal realization claim has no determinate premise.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:regular-circuit-inference
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The theorem is conditional on ProbeID returning a fixed regular circuit with locally constant branch, nonzero denominators, and positive delta-method variance.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Normality, plug-in variance consistency, and Wald coverage are asserted only on a fixed regular returned-circuit stratum, not uniformly across rank changes, branch ties, or vanishing variance.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Examples 7–8 explicitly recover every entry of an unknown normalized matrix process from spanning state preparations and effects; Proposition 6 characterizes MIC for separable branches, and Theorem 1 is restricted to Markovian models.
The paper requires positivity of observed-law cells in \(\mathcal M^+(G)\) and gives a sound-and-complete gID algorithm reducing single c-components to classical ID subproblems.
The primary abstract states a necessary-and-sufficient graphical condition and an algorithm for identifying arbitrary interventional distributions in recursive semi-Markovian models.
The paper defines ADMG nested Markov structure through kernels obtained by fixing, proves the latent-DAG margin relationship, and connects the fixing operation to identifiable causal effects.
The paper gives a sound-and-complete gID procedure for arbitrary collections of observational and experimental distributions, not coarse local input-output probe contractions.
The paper estimates g-identifiable effects from observational and randomized-intervention distributions and imposes positive cell probabilities for its discrete multi-source regime.
The paper derives influence-function and weight-based estimators for broad hidden-variable DAG classes, including front-door settings, from observational-law identification functionals.
